Grace / team —

Looping in a quick technical summary so Novus has the constraints before the kickoff:

Streaming behavior (runtime defaults):
- Default chunk size: ~512 tokens; we can lower to 256 for more frequent partials if Novus needs finer-grained updates.
- Each stream chunk includes metadata: sequence index, partial_json fragment (for structured-output assembly), and finality flag. See redwood_feature_enablement_schema_v1.json -> streaming.streaming_chunk_format.
- If a single response exceeds the configured max_tokens limit, runtime will emit a partial chunk and set continuation=true; client should concat partial_json segments in order.

Function/tool-call semantics:
- We treat function-call delivery as at-least-once by default. Customers should implement idempotency keys on their endpoint.
- The schema includes optional fields: call.idempotency_key (string) and call.attempt (int) for tracking retries.
- For synchronous tool calls we can support blocking calls up to 10s; for longer tasks we recommend queue-based webhook with async ack.

Structured output / schema notes:
- The schema enforces a top-level object: {"output_version","actions":[],"metadata":{}}. Each action must include {"action_name","params","confidence"}.
- For QA we suggest adding a small canonicalizer step in Novus's adapter that maps our action names to your internal action ids.

Implementation owners / low-level tasks I propose:
- Adapter + JSON assembler (Dev Patel) — map streaming partials -> final JSON and implement idempotency header handling.
- Unit + integration tests (Monica Patel) — end-to-end test harness that replays sample prompts and validates structured-output.
- Observability config (Dylan Brooks) — add tracing hooks and token-cost metrics for the canary.

I’ll bring a short checklist to the kickoff with example curl commands.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Engineer, Inference Runtime

- Dev to implement adapter skeleton and idempotency header support, PR to internal repo by 2026-06-25 (Dev Patel)

Canary strategy (proposed):
- 10% internal traffic seeded against Novus adapter for the first 48 hours; collect metrics on latency, function errors, and malformed structured-output.
- If >0.6% malformed-output or >3% function-call failures, automatic rollback to non-structured fallback.

Elena — could you please share the sample payload URLs or endpoint docs ahead of the call if possible? That will let Dev and Monica prep stubs.

Thanks — I’ll follow up post-kickoff with the updated schema and a short test plan.

Best,
Grace
